result.title: Causal Optimal-Transport Attention: Positional Priors and Length Extrapolation
result.summary: Causal masking obstructs the column balancing used by optimal-transport (OT) attention. We study a prefix-consistent unbalanced operator and characterize the positional prior it induces. Under bounded scores, for any fixed balancing strength $ρ<1$, its fixed point dilutes attention: every fixed window receives a vanishing share as the context grows. For constant scores, we derive an exact scale-invariant prior. We then classify positional encodings by whether their distant attention mass remains bounded away from one. Discrete window-mass bounds quantify the finite-length dilution of summable log-distance priors near exponent one. Preregistered experiments with 25M- and 100M-parameter language models establish improved loss extrapolation over softmax; exploratory comparisons favor an explicit distance bias at a fraction of the cost. CABLE outperforms RoPE with evaluation-time YaRN on every seed at three training lengths. Changing only the bias beyond the training length moves long-context loss in the predicted direction on all 30 tested checkpoints. Even with exponents constrained above one, many heads approach the summability boundary during training. A margin selected by prior-only calculations for a specified window, length range and growth tolerance controls distant-mass growth in the tested setting. These results connect loss extrapolation to positional decay over the lengths actually evaluated.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究因果掩码下最优传输注意力的失衡算子及其诱导的位置先验，推导有界分数下注意力随上下文增长被稀释、常数分数下尺度不变先验等结论，并据此分类位置编码、提出 CABLE，用 25M/100M 语言模型的预注册实验检验长度外推。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本、不涉及视觉推理，但其关于注意力结构、远距注意力质量衰减与位置偏置如何影响长度外推的分析，可供核查 LVR 中位置与注意力结构对长序列推理状态的影响。
